newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg Q2 global volume up 14 percent.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg Q2 global volume up 14 percent.

text.p: Kellogg Co, which posted stronger than expected second quarter results, said Friday its global sales volume rose 14 percent in the second quarter, including Lender's Bagels that was acquired in December 1996.
Excluding Lender's, global volume was up eight percent.

"Our second quarter results were driven by cereal volume increases in all four of our global operating areas, continued double-digit volume growth in our convenience foods business, and savings from our ongoing cost-reduction initiatives," Arnold Langbo, chairman, said in a statement.
Kellogg's operating areas are North America, Europe, Asia/Pacific and Latin America.

Earlier, Kellogg reported second quarter earnings before a $0.04 charge of $0.83 a share, above the First Call consensus of $0.73 a share, and well above depressed year-ago results of $0.45 a share before a charge.

He added that the company's strategy, which includes "aggressive development" of cereal and convenience food brand equities, new products and improved efficiency, positions Kellogg for continued growth.

"Volume growth during the second quarter was enhanced by solid performances from our two newest U.S. cereal products, Kellogg's Honey Crunch Corn Flakes and Kellogg's Cocoa Frosted Flakes," Langbo said. "These successful products are part of our company-wide initiative to enhance long-term growth by further developing and leveraging our core equities."

He added that Kellogg is expanding its Rice Krispies franchise, rolling out in the United States Kellogg's Razzle Dazzle Rice Krispies cereal and a chocolate-chip flavor of Kellogg's Rice Krispies Treats squares.
